title: Client-side Exposure Manager: SDK helpers for progressive canary, shadowing, and auto-rollback
creator: Anika Patel
description: Build an opinionated client-side SDK layer (Exposure Manager) that provides ergonomic helpers for progressive exposure (canaries and A/B), shadowing traffic to new model variants, and policy-driven automatic rollbacks. This work complements server-side rollout primitives by enabling service owners to perform safe, reproducible staged promotions without embedding rollout logic into application code. The SDK should integrate with Redwood's control-plane endpoints, be idempotent for retry-safe workflows, and respect permission checks from the authz service.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a single ExposureManager class with declarative APIs for startCanary(), startABTest(), and startShadow(), each accepting a rollout policy DSL string or JSON (SDK transforms to control-plane contract).
All SDK operations include an idempotency_token parameter and retry semantics: duplicate start*() calls with same idempotency_token are no-ops and return the same rollout handle.
ExposureManager fetches and validates the caller's permissions before creating traffic rules; calls fail fast with a 403-like error when the caller lacks rollout.create permission.
Shadowing sends a copy of live request through the shadow() path without impacting production response latency; SDK provides optional sampling and bandwidth throttling knobs.
Auto-rollback hooks: SDK registers local health callbacks (latency/error thresholds) and can trigger a control-plane rollback API when policy violations persist for configured windows.
SDK emits structured telemetry events (rollout.start, rollout.update, rollout.rollback, rollout.complete) to the Redwood telemetry endpoint and includes trace/context propagation headers.
End-to-end integration tests demonstrate canary -> promote and canary -> auto-rollback when injected regressions cause metric degradation.
Documentation page and quickstart example (Node + Python) included in the PR and linked from Console rollout docs.
notes: 2025-03-01 - Anika Patel: Initial ticket created after sprint planning. Goal: unblock platform teams who requested lightweight rollout helpers for microservices.

2025-03-02 - Marco Ruiz: Spike completed for idempotency semantics; verified passing idempotency_token to control plane solves duplicate-create races. Chosen approach: client generates a UUID v4 by default and accepts caller-overrides.

2025-03-03 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented early ExposureManager prototype (Node). Basic startCanary() translates local policy DSL to control-plane manifest v2 and calls /rollouts API. Need to wire authz calls to obtain effective permissions; currently using service-account scope.
2025-03-04 - QA: Added tests for shadow sampling and confirmed that sampling is applied before network send to control-plane to keep cost predictable.

2025-03-05 - Security: Raised that policy DSL contains rule expressions; plan to run static validation and server-side sanitize to avoid eval-like injection risks. Security review flagged and added to labels.
comments: Priya Shah (PM) 2025-03-02: Please ensure the SDK surface supports both declarative DSL and a low-level manifest passthrough for platform teams that already construct rollout manifests.

Diego Martinez (SRE) 2025-03-03: For auto-rollback triggers, prefer a push model where SDK posts summarized metrics to control-plane rather than making control decisions locally; offers better observability. We should support both modes, default to control-plane decisioning.

Lina Zhou (Design) 2025-03-04: UX note — expose an easy 'preview' API that returns estimated traffic split and expected latency impact for chosen sampling/bandwidth settings. This will reduce operator errors.
Marco Ruiz 2025-03-05: Action item — add integration test harness with traffic-generator that can simulate 10k RPS and inject regressions to validate rollback timing.
